**Verdict: merge-ready.** Second look under the safety floor, independent of the author. Built on a merged tree (head f1ed9b6e7 + current main; the trial merge is clean).

Evidence run here (`--no-fail-fast`, every binary reported):
- `tool_numbers`: 17 passed. `mcp_tool_number`: 8 passed. `tool_import_modes`: 9 passed. `posting`: 10 passed. `setup_mounts_post`: 1 passed.
- `microarc_test_part`: 3 passed, 1 failed - `a_wrapped_op_on_the_test_part_posts_wrapped_a` is the known #2483 line-count red on main, and the new `wrapped_fixture_keeps_golden_tool_numbers` pin passes.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib tool_number`: 2 passed.

Code reading: creation and import take the lowest unused number through `next_free`, so no two new tools can share a `T` word; the clash law still refuses a shared number by name. Legacy files freeze at load to the list position every older document posted, so a pre-#2442 project keeps its exact G-code after one load-and-save; the `numbers()` fallback only serves in-memory fixtures. The `MAX` bound is shared-sanity only; each control post keeps refusing past its own table. The MCP surface adds the number tools with `area:mcp` truth, and the skill row change is a process change declared right: `Process change: yes` is in the body and `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` is untouched.

Labels: `merge-ready` stands as the author set it; this comment adds the independent floor marker.
